correctness.rationale: For each n=3,...,10 the independent check.py reconstructs the complete 2^n-by-2^(n-3) distinct-subsequence incidence, checks all witness codewords against every output (list count at most 2), and evaluates every rational dual inequality. With weights w_y>=0 and s_x=max(0,1-sum_{y subseq x} w_y), the inequality |C|<=2 sum_y w_y + sum_x s_x follows for all feasible codes. The eight exact upper bounds 2,3,4,4,4,22/3,659/60,2693/180 have integer floors equal to the eight supplied feasible sizes 2,3,4,4,4,7,10,14. This is an exhaustive finite proof in the specified range, not a claim based on floating-point solver success.

value.rationale: The first eight lengths in the new k=3,t=2 deletion-hypergraph packing problem form a natural finite benchmark for a model recently studied asymptotically. The exact plateau at size four through n=7 and first jump to seven at n=8 cannot be read off from asymptotic existence bounds; rational dual witnesses make the results checkable independent of optimization software. This is a mathematically motivated exact short-blocklength profile with matching nontrivial certificates, not merely a generic formula substitution or unverified solver table.
